title: Sketch of a Witch of Agnesi Type Curve y = x/(x^2 + 1)
originalTopic: Combining symmetry, extrema and asymptotes for a graph
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Before plotting y = x/(x^2 + 1), predict its symmetry, its highest and lowest points, and its end behavior, then confirm that a window such as [-4, 4] by [-1.5, 1.5] shows all of it.
finalAnswer: \text{odd symmetry; max } \tfrac{1}{2} \text{ at } x = 1; \min = -\tfrac{1}{2} \text{ at } x = -1; \text{horizontal asymptote } y = 0

steps.title: Test symmetry and the domain
steps.explanation: The function is odd, so its graph is a half-turn of itself about the origin, and the denominator never vanishes, meaning the curve is smooth on the whole real line.
steps.why: Odd symmetry halves the work: plotting x >= 0 determines the rest, and it also guarantees the maximum and minimum have equal magnitudes.

steps.title: Differentiate to find the extreme values
steps.explanation: The derivative vanishes at x = plus or minus 1, is positive between them and negative outside, so x = 1 gives the peak f(1) = 1/2 and x = -1 the trough f(-1) = -1/2.
steps.why: The sign chart of the derivative converts the guess of symmetry into exact turning-point coordinates.

steps.title: Analyze end behavior
steps.explanation: The denominator grows one degree faster than the numerator, so both arms flatten onto the x-axis, which is a horizontal asymptote approached from above on the right and below on the left.
steps.why: Degree comparison predicts the asymptote, and there are no vertical asymptotes to worry about.

steps.title: Select the window
steps.explanation: The extreme values are only plus or minus 0.5, so a y-range of [-1.5, 1.5] shows the bumps at a readable height while the x-range of 8 units reveals the flattening onto y = 0.
steps.why: A default [-10, 10] by [-10, 10] window would flatten this short curve into an almost invisible line along the axis.
